title: Samson's Gate: 60 km Uphill?
author: QUILL
notes: Gaza-Hebron straight-line ~60 km, Hebron ~900 m higher. 'Facing Hebron' nuance is the single not-proven line (beat 6).

beats.text: Samson carried a gate sixty kilometres uphill?
At midnight, in Gaza. But the gate isn't the strangest part.
Judges 16: Samson lifts the doors of Gaza's gate, posts and bar.
Bar and all, he carries it off on his shoulders.
Destination: the hill facing Hebron, about 60 kilometres away and 900 metres uphill.
beats.say: Destination: the hill facing HEB-ron, about sixty kilometres away and nine hundred metres uphill.

beats.text: Not proven: the exact hill. The Hebrew can mean 'facing' Hebron, not at it.
beats.say: Not proven: the exact hill. The Hebrew can mean 'facing' HEB-ron, not at it.

beats.text: But he ends up blinded, grinding grain in a Gaza prison.
Philistines gather in Dagon's temple, with about 3,000 on the roof.
beats.say: FILL-iss-teens gather in DAY-gon's temple, with about three thousand on the roof.
beats.label: ~3,000 ON THE ROOF

beats.text: Samson pushes the two middle pillars, and the building comes down.
Zorah to Gaza is nearly 60 kilometres. His world is small; his legend is big.
beats.say: ZOR-ah to Gaza is nearly sixty kilometres. His world is small; his legend is big.

beats.text: Samson carried a gate sixty kilometres uphill? Legend, or memory?

youtube.title: Samson's Gate: 60 km Uphill? 🗺️ #shorts
youtube.description:
From Gaza's gate to the hill facing Hebron: roughly 60 km straight-line, and about 900 metres uphill. Legend or memory?
The exact hill is not proven; the Hebrew can mean 'facing' Hebron.
